mpm_correlation.title: MPM MODEL vs FIRING TABLE
mpm_correlation.subtitle: 7 charges · 722 points · R² = 0.9998 · aggregate RMS 56 m (< 0.4% of range)
mpm_correlation.description: Scatter plot of MPM-predicted range vs Firing Table range for all 7 charges. Dashed 1:1 line shows perfect agreement.

mpm_errors.title: MPM RANGE ERROR — PER CHARGE
mpm_errors.subtitle: numbers above each box: per-charge RMS in metres
mpm_errors.description: Box-and-whisker plot of range error (MPM minus FT) per charge. Red dots are outliers. Numbers above boxes are per-charge RMS.

mpm_tof.title: TIME OF FLIGHT — ALL CHARGES
mpm_tof.subtitle: MPM reproduced within 0.3 s across all charges
mpm_tof.description: Time of flight vs range for all 7 charges. Each charge shows a curve that bends back at maximum range (high-angle fire). MPM matches FT within 0.3 s.

mpm_trajectory_fan.title: TRAJECTORY FAMILY — CHARGE 7W
mpm_trajectory_fan.subtitle: MV = 568 m/s · apogee sweep across QE range
mpm_trajectory_fan.description: Family of 5 representative trajectories for Charge 7W at different quadrant elevations, showing how apogee and range change with QE.

roll_decoupled.title: ROLL-DECOUPLED MOTION — BODY vs NOSE SPIN
roll_decoupled.subtitle: body keeps gyroscopic stability · nose Earth-locked for canard steering
roll_decoupled.description: Comparison of body spin (p_b) and nose spin (p_n) after bearing engagement. Body maintains constant spin ~-1100 rad/s for gyroscopic stability. Nose section is braked to ~0 rad/s by alternator for Earth-fixed canard steering.

nose_spin.label: NOSE spin p_n (alternator-braked)
nose_spin.behavior: Braked to zero after bearing engagement

roll_decoupled_drift.title: WHY ROLL-DECOUPLING MATTERS FOR STEERING
roll_decoupled_drift.subtitle: rotating canards average to zero · decoupled canards integrate into real correction
roll_decoupled_drift.description: Two-panel comparison showing why roll-decoupling is essential. Left: lateral acceleration — coupled canards oscillate at body spin rate (~±0.93 m/s²), averaging to zero net effect; decoupled canards produce steady ~0.2 m/s² lateral acceleration. Right: net lateral velocity — coupled canards produce zero net velocity; decoupled canards build to ~4.5 m/s by 25 s.

sixdof_aoa.title: TOTAL ANGLE-OF-ATTACK ENVELOPE — 7W QE 600
sixdof_aoa.subtitle: peak AoA at apogee, damped to <0.5° near impact
sixdof_aoa.description: Envelope of total angle of attack over the full trajectory for Charge 7W at QE 600 mil. Shows initial nutation oscillations (0-5 s), gradual growth to peak ~1.0° at apogee (~27 s), then damping to ~0.3° near impact (~48 s).

sixdof_epicyclic.title: EPICYCLIC MOTION — α vs β (first 250 ms)
sixdof_epicyclic.subtitle: nutation + precession spiral — structurally invisible to 3DOF MPM
sixdof_epicyclic.description: Phase-plane plot of angle of attack (α) vs side-slip (β) for the first 250 ms of flight. Shows the characteristic epicyclic spiral pattern from combined nutation and precession. The spiral damps inward over time. This motion is captured by 6DOF but invisible to 3DOF MPM models.

sixdof_rates.title: BODY-FRAME ANGULAR RATES — p / q / r
sixdof_rates.subtitle: gyroscopic spin (p) dominates; pitch and yaw oscillate with coning
sixdof_rates.description: Body-frame angular rates over the full trajectory for Charge 7W at QE 600 mil. Axial spin (p) dominates at ~-1130 rad/s and remains nearly constant. Pitch (q) and yaw (r) rates are near zero with small coning oscillations invisible at this scale.

sixdof_vs_mpm.title: 6DOF vs MPM — 7W @ QE 600 mil
sixdof_vs_mpm.subtitle: 6DOF adds lateral drift from spin and yaw-of-repose
sixdof_vs_mpm.description: Two-panel comparison of 6DOF (full attitude) vs MPM (3DOF + corrections) for Charge 7W at QE 600 mil. Left panel: altitude vs down-range — both models produce nearly identical vertical trajectories (curves overlap). Right panel: cross-range vs down-range — 6DOF captures spin drift (~430 m at 14 km) while MPM has no lateral model (0 m cross-range).

right_panel.title: Cross-Range (Spin Drift)
right_panel.key_difference: 6DOF captures ~430 m spin drift at 14 km that MPM misses entirely
